title: SCIM: telemetry-driven user expiry orchestration with safe rollback
creator: Ava Chou
body:
Summary: We need a safe, observable orchestration for SCIM-driven user lifecycle expiration (soft-suspend -> final removal) that uses telemetry signals to gate progress and supports idempotent retries, tenant-scoped rate limiting, and admin-initiated rollbacks. This ticket implements the orchestration layer, metrics/audit events, and an operator UI hook so support can intervene during the grace window.

Background: Multiple customers have reported accidental mass-deprovisions when third-party IdPs return stale group deltas or when SCIM delta jobs are retried aggressively. Existing SCIM workers perform deletions and emit basic audit logs, but we lack a standardized state machine and telemetry gates to safely escalate from soft-suspend to permanent removal.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement a three-state user lifecycle: ACTIVE -> SOFT_SUSPENDED (tombstone candidate, reversible) -> PENDING_DELETE (finalization) -> DELETED, with configurable grace window per org.
- All state transitions must emit audit events with trace IDs and user/actor/tenant fields (events: scim.user.suspend.requested, scim.user.suspend.applied, scim.user.delete.requested, scim.user.delete.completed).
- Provisioning orchestration must be idempotent: retries from SCIM webhook or background job should not cause double-deletes or inconsistent group membership.
- Add telemetry gates that prevent promotion from SOFT_SUSPENDED to PENDING_DELETE when: recent failures for tenant > 5% over 1h OR audit-sampled restore rate > 0.5% over 24h OR active rollback flag set by SRE/product.
- Tenant-scoped rate limiting for finalization: at most X final deletions per minute per tenant (configurable), with circuit-breaker that pauses finalization on high error rate and surfaces runbook.
- Integrate with Console: admin-facing list of users in SOFT_SUSPENDED with restore button and timeline.
- End-to-end tests + integration test against Okta/OneLogin sandbox and a fault-injection harness.

Proposed design:
1) Orchestration state machine lives in identity-service: lightweight DynamoDB table (or Postgres table namespace) containing user_id, tenant_id, state, state_version, last_updated_at, tombstone_expires_at, pending_ops (dedup token). To avoid race conditions with concurrent SCIM deltas, include an epoch-based state_version and require compare-and-set updates.
2) When SCIM delta indicates user removal, mark SOFT_SUSPENDED with tombstone_expires_at = now + tenant_grace_period and emit scim.user.suspend.applied audit event. Do not remove group links yet.
3) Background finalizer worker scans SOFT_SUSPENDED records whose tombstone_expires_at <= now and attempts to transition to PENDING_DELETE after evaluating telemetry gates. Telemetry gates implemented as queries against metrics store (Prometheus/Influx) and recent audit logs.
4) Finalizer performs tenant-scoped batching and uses a token bucket to limit deletion throughput. Each deletion is recorded with a unique op_id; deletion idempotency achieved by storing op_id in pending_ops and using idempotent delete endpoints to external identity providers.
5) If finalizer sees high error rate or gate triggered, it will pause for tenant (exponential backoff with jitter) and mark a pause_reason in the orchestration table. Admins can resume or rollback from Console.
6) Rollback path: within the grace window, Console can hit an endpoint to move user from SOFT_SUSPENDED back to ACTIVE. For PENDING_DELETE we allow a short undo window (30 minutes) if the finalization job has not yet processed the external delete step. Once external delete succeeded, we emit scim.user.delete.completed and only a manual account-restore (reprovision) is possible.

Telemetry & auditing:
- Metrics to add: counter scim.user.suspend.count{tenant}, scim.user.finalize.attempts{tenant}, scim.user.finalize.failures{tenant}, scim.user.rollback.count{tenant}, scim.user.restore.count{tenant}.
- Histograms: scim.finalizer.duration (ms).
- Alerts: tenant-specific alert when finalize_failures/attempts > 0.1 over 15m (configurable) and global incident if many tenants show elevated failure rates.
- Audit events must include correlation_id (trace id) and link to the Console action event. Store audit events in the existing audit-log pipeline and ensure retention aligns with compliance policies.

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Duplicate SCIM deltas: use dedup token and state_version CAS to avoid double-applying transition; idempotent calls to external IdP.
- Partial external failures (Okta times out): finalizer marks item PENDING_DELETE with last_error and retries with backoff; expose last_error in Console.
- Large tenant blasts: tenant-scoped throttling and circuit-breaker to prevent noisy-neighbor impact.
- Operator mistakes: soft-suspend grace window and explicit restore action in Console.

Migration & rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement state machine and soft-suspend path for 5 pilot tenants (low-risk) and enable verbose logging + feature flag.
- Phase 2: add finalizer job behind feature flag; run as read-only dry-run (simulate finalization) for 2 weeks and collect metrics.
- Phase 3: enable finalization for more tenants with conservative rate limits; open 72h rollback window for first 50 tenants.
- Phase 4: full rollout and deprecation of old immediate-delete path.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for state transitions and CAS semantics.
- Integration tests against a mocked Okta SCIM server covering success, 429, 5xx, and network failure.
- Chaos test: interrupt finalize worker mid-batch and verify idempotency and correct resume.
- Manual end-to-end with an Okta sandbox tenant and Console restore flow.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- identity-service: orchestration table, API endpoints for suspend/restore/finalize (Diego).
- finalizer-worker: tenant-scoped batching, telemetry gating, circuit-breaker (SRE pairing with Diego).
- console: admin UI for soft-suspended users and restore button (FRONTEND ticket to be created).
- metrics: Prometheus instrumenters + dashboards (Nikhil).
- docs: runbook + runbook play for high-failure tenant (PM/Support).

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/SCIM-telemetry-expiry (internal)
- Draft schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity/pull/412
- Example Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/SCIM-Console-Mocks

Open questions:
1) Should tombstone_expires_at be tenant-configurable via Console configs or only via org policy? (PM preference is per-tenant config behind RBAC).
2) Where to persist last_error and pause_reason: orchestration table or separate incidents table? Storing with orchestration row simplifies debugging but increases row size.
3) Do we need per-tenant SLAs for finalization latency? current assumption: best-effort within 24h for normal tenants.

Next steps (short term):
- Implement orchestration schema migration and unit tests (Diego) by 2026-02-28.
- Create finalizer skeleton and metric counters in a feature branch (Diego + SRE) by 2026-03-05.
- Schedule review with Security and Compliance for audit retention and event shape (Ava to schedule).
